The story is written in the format of a sparse dramatic script, relying almost entirely on dialogue and minimal stage directions to convey emotional tension. As a result, it lacks sensory details that paint a tangible picture of the environment. There are no descriptions of colors, shapes, scents (like the smell of the café or the rain), tastes (neither character actually drinks their coffee), textures, or background sounds. Apart from a brief mention in the dialogue that the coffee is "hot" and will get "cold," and the visual cue of it starting to rain at the very end, the five senses are largely unstimulated, leaving the physical setting very bare and abstract.
